text.p: Following are the main stories from Monday morning's Slovenia newspapers:

- Marjan Podobnik, leader of the conservative People's Party which last month formed a coalition with the dominant centre-left Liberal Democrats, was seen as the most important political personality of the month, an opinion poll showed.

- Foreign minister Zoran Thaler said Slovenia's parliament should ratify an association agreement with the European Union, signed in June last year, as soon as possible, but no later than in the first half of this year.
- Telephone maker Iskratel, 48-percent owned by Germany's Siemens , said its profit rose by 15 percent in 1996 as the company expanded its production, three quarters of which were exported.
- Analysts said President Milan Kucan was almost certain to be re-elected when his term expires at the end of the year unless the rightist "Spring" parties decided to nominate a rival candidate.
- Slovenia's national airline Adria Airways may have to reduce its workforce in order to repay its debts and start operating at a profit, the company's supervisory board said.
- Some 70 million tolars ($0.5 million) were collected at a charity show on Friday for the construction of a new health clinic for children. REUTER
